title: Cómo la inteligencia artificial está reinventando la experiencia de empleado: el nuevo motor de productividad, talento e innovación en las empresas
summary: La inteligencia artificial está transformando la experiencia de empleado: automatiza tareas, personaliza entornos y mejora productividad, talento y bienestar. Descubre claves, beneficios y tendencias.
body_text: Cómo la inteligencia artificial está transformando la experiencia de empleado en las empresas La inteligencia artificial está cambiando la forma en la que las personas interactúan con la tecnología dentro de las organizaciones. Estamos pasando de entornos donde el empleado tenía que adaptarse a las herramientas a modelos donde las herramientas entienden el contexto, anticipan necesidades y simplifican el trabajo diario. El verdadero cambio no está solo en automatizar tareas, sino en eliminar fricciones para que las personas puedan dedicar más tiempo a innovar, colaborar y aportar valor. Qué es la inteligencia artificial aplicada a la experiencia de empleado y por qué es clave para las organizaciones Es la aplicación de capacidades inteligentes para mejorar la relación de los empleados con su entorno de trabajo durante todo su ciclo de vida en la empresa. Se ha convertido en un factor estratégico porque la experiencia de empleado impacta directamente en la productividad, el compromiso, la capacidad de innovación y la atracción de talento. Hoy, las organizaciones más competitivas son aquellas capaces de combinar tecnología avanzada con una experiencia humana excelente. Cómo integrar la inteligencia artificial en los procesos internos para mejorar la experiencia de empleado La clave es identificar los momentos que generan más fricción y aplicar la IA donde realmente aporta valor. Un buen ejemplo son los portales personalizados que combinan IA generativa, experiencia digital y automatización. Los empleados pueden consultar el estado de sus dispositivos, ejecutar acciones de autocuidado o conocer incidencias que se han resuelto automáticamente, mientras que los equipos técnicos disponen de una visión completa de la salud del entorno tecnológico. Cuando la tecnología es capaz de resolver problemas antes de que el usuario tenga que reportarlos, la experiencia cambia radicalmente. Beneficios de la inteligencia artificial en la experiencia de empleado: productividad, satisfacción y desarrollo profesional La IA mejora la productividad al reducir tiempos de búsqueda, automatizar tareas repetitivas y facilitar el acceso al conocimiento. Aumenta la satisfacción porque simplifica la relación con la tecnología y ofrece experiencias más fluidas y personalizadas. Además, acelera el desarrollo profesional al facilitar formación adaptada, acceso al conocimiento experto y acompañamiento continuo en el aprendizaje de nuevas capacidades. Cómo la inteligencia artificial impulsa la personalización de la experiencia de empleado en grandes empresas La personalización es uno de los mayores avances que aporta la IA. Permite adaptar servicios, contenidos y experiencias al perfil, rol, necesidades y contexto de cada empleado. Esto es especialmente relevante en organizaciones globales, donde es necesario ofrecer una experiencia homogénea pero al mismo tiempo cercana y relevante para cada persona. La IA permite combinar ambas cosas: escala y personalización. Impacto de la inteligencia artificial en la gestión del talento y las nuevas formas de trabajo La IA está impulsando modelos más centrados en habilidades y capacidades que en puestos tradicionales. Ayuda a identificar talento, recomendar itinerarios de desarrollo y facilitar la movilidad interna. Pero además está dando lugar a nuevas formas de colaboración entre personas y sistemas inteligentes. Con la llegada de la IA agéntica, los empleados podrán apoyarse en agentes especializados capaces de ejecutar tareas, coordinar procesos y aportar conocimiento experto. Un profesional podrá solicitar a un agente que prepare una propuesta comercial personalizada, genere un análisis de riesgos o recopile información relevante en cuestión de segundos. Cómo la inteligencia artificial mejora la toma de decisiones y el bienestar del empleado La IA permite transformar grandes volúmenes de información en decisiones más rápidas y precisas. Gracias a la combinación de inteligencia artificial, observabilidad y automatización, las organizaciones pueden detectar incidencias antes de que afecten al empleado y actuar de forma preventiva. Imaginemos que el sistema identifica que una persona tiene una reunión crítica en pocas horas. De forma automática puede revisar el estado del dispositivo, optimizar el rendimiento, verificar la conectividad y corregir posibles anomalías antes de que se conviertan en un problema. La mejor incidencia es la que nunca llega a producirse. Cómo la inteligencia artificial está cambiando las herramientas de trabajo y la relación con la tecnología Las herramientas están evolucionando desde interfaces complejas hacia experiencias conversacionales, intuitivas y proactivas. Ya no se trata únicamente de responder preguntas. La IA es capaz de acompañar al usuario mientras trabaja, guiándole paso a paso en procesos complejos, facilitando el aprendizaje de nuevas aplicaciones y reduciendo significativamente la curva de adopción tecnológica. La tecnología deja de ser una barrera para convertirse en un acompañante inteligente. Principales retos de la inteligencia artificial en la experiencia de empleado y cómo superarlos Los principales desafíos son la confianza, la calidad de los datos, la integración tecnológica y la adopción por parte de los usuarios. La respuesta pasa por combinar innovación con responsabilidad. Es fundamental construir soluciones transparentes, seguras y éticas, acompañadas de programas de formación y gestión del cambio que ayuden a las personas a comprender y aprovechar todo el potencial de la IA. La adopción no se consigue imponiendo tecnología, sino demostrando utilidad. Cómo la inteligencia artificial refuerza el posicionamiento de Telefónica como empresa innovadora y centrada en las personas La IA permite a Telefónica demostrar que la innovación tecnológica y la orientación a las personas son dos elementos inseparables. Al incorporar capacidades avanzadas de automatización, asistentes inteligentes, experiencia digital y agentes especializados, podemos crear entornos de trabajo más eficientes, personalizados y atractivos. La verdadera diferenciación no estará en quién dispone de más inteligencia artificial, sino en quién es capaz de utilizarla para potenciar mejor el talento humano. Tendencias de inteligencia artificial en la experiencia de empleado que marcarán el futuro Estamos entrando en una nueva etapa en la que la IA dejará de ser una herramienta para convertirse en un ecosistema de agentes inteligentes que trabajarán junto a las personas. Veremos asistentes capaces de comprender contexto, objetivos y prioridades; agentes especializados que colaborarán entre sí para resolver tareas complejas; y entornos digitales que se adaptarán dinámicamente a cada empleado. La experiencia de trabajo será cada vez más predictiva e invisible. Los sistemas identificarán necesidades antes de que aparezcan, prepararán automáticamente el entorno tecnológico, propondrán acciones y eliminarán fricciones de forma autónoma. El futuro no será tener más tecnología, sino una tecnología tan integrada y natural que prácticamente desaparecerá de nuestra atención. La inteligencia artificial actuará como una capa invisible que amplificará nuestras capacidades, liberándonos de tareas operativas para centrarnos en aquello que nos hace únicos: la creatividad, el criterio, la empatía y la capacidad de transformar ideas en impacto real. En este contexto, la apuesta de Telefónica por la inteligencia artificial y la experiencia de empleado se enmarca en una ambición aún mayor: convertirse en la mejor vía de acceso de los ciudadanos a las tecnologías digitales. Para ello, la compañía impulsa una transformación basada en la innovación, la excelencia de servicio y el desarrollo del talento, consolidando su liderazgo en Europa, reforzando su competitividad global y situando a las personas en el centro de un modelo donde la tecnología no solo mejora la eficiencia, sino que genera confianza, progreso y valor sostenible.

title: ServiceNow Review 2026: Honest Pros and Cons
summary: Explore our 2026 ServiceNow review covering features, pricing, AI capabilities, implementation, pros, cons, and how it compares with modern Slack-native alternatives like Unthread.
body_text: ServiceNow has dominated enterprise IT service management for over two decades, and its position in 2026 reflects both the strengths that built that dominance and the limitations that increasingly frustrate modern IT, HR, and operations teams. The platform has evolved from its ITSM roots into a comprehensive enterprise service management suite, expanding into HR service delivery, security operations, and dozens of specialized modules. This evolution has created a system of remarkable breadth and capability, yet also introduced complexity that many organizations struggle to justify for their internal support needs. For organizations evaluating whether ServiceNow fits their internal support needs, the honest assessment requires looking beyond marketing materials to understand where the platform delivers genuine value and where it creates unnecessary complexity. The emergence of Slack-native helpdesk solutions has fundamentally changed the competitive landscape. Teams that once assumed ServiceNow was their only enterprise-grade option now have alternatives that meet employees where they already work, reducing the friction of separate portals and training overhead. This review examines ServiceNow's current capabilities, honest pros and cons, and how it compares to modern alternatives for internal IT, HR, and employee support workflows in 2026. Key Takeaways ServiceNow remains the enterprise ITSM heavyweight but comes with significant complexity trade-offs. Organizations with large IT budgets and dedicated admin teams benefit most, while mid-market companies may find the platform more complex than their internal support workflows require. Implementation timelines and costs can exceed initial projections. Larger deployments may require specialized consultants and ongoing administrative overhead that smaller IT teams may not be prepared to maintain. The Now Platform's AI capabilities have matured but require substantial configuration. Unlike purpose-built AI agents that work out of the box, ServiceNow's AI features demand significant setup, training data, and ongoing tuning to deliver meaningful ticket deflection. Slack-native alternatives have emerged as serious competitors for internal support teams. Organizations already running their operations in Slack can now access enterprise-grade ticketing, workflow automation, and AI resolution without the context-switching that ServiceNow requires. ServiceNow excels at cross-enterprise workflow orchestration but creates friction for day-to-day employee requests. The platform shines when coordinating complex processes across multiple departments but adds unnecessary overhead for simple IT, HR, or finance requests that employees submit daily. Understanding What ServiceNow is Used For in 2026 ServiceNow started as an IT service management platform but has evolved into a comprehensive enterprise service management suite. The Now Platform now spans IT operations management (ITOM), customer service management (CSM), human resources service delivery (HRSD), security operations, and dozens of specialized modules for everything from legal service delivery to workplace facilities management. Primary use cases for ServiceNow in 2026 include: IT Service Management (ITSM) coordinating incident response, problem management, change requests, and service catalog fulfillment across large IT organizations HR Service Delivery handling employee onboarding, benefits administration, payroll inquiries, and policy questions through structured workflows IT Operations Management monitoring infrastructure health, managing cloud resources, and automating remediation for production issues Security Operations orchestrating incident response, vulnerability management, and compliance workflows across security teams Enterprise Asset Management tracking hardware, software licenses, and IT assets throughout their lifecycle The platform's core strength lies in its ability to connect these disparate functions through a unified data model. When an employee submits an access request, ServiceNow can coordinate approvals across IT, security, and HR without manual handoffs between separate systems. However, this breadth comes at a cost. Organizations frequently deploy ServiceNow for one use case, then find themselves pressured to expand into adjacent modules to justify the investment. What began as an ITSM deployment becomes an enterprise-wide platform initiative requiring dedicated development teams, governance committees, and ongoing consulting relationships. For internal support teams specifically, the question becomes whether ServiceNow's enterprise capabilities justify the overhead when simpler solutions can handle IT and HR help desk functions with faster setup and lower administrative burden. Evaluating ServiceNow's Role as a Leading ITSM Software in 2026 ServiceNow's ITSM module remains the benchmark against which other IT service management tools are measured. The platform offers mature implementations of ITIL processes, including incident management, problem management, change management, release management, and configuration management with an integrated configuration management database (CMDB). Incident and Problem Management Capabilities ServiceNow's incident management provides structured workflows for logging, categorizing, prioritizing, and resolving IT issues. The platform supports multi-tier assignment groups, escalation rules based on SLA timelines, and integration with monitoring tools that can automatically create incidents when infrastructure issues are detected. Problem management builds on incident data to identify root causes of recurring issues. ServiceNow can correlate related incidents, track known errors, and manage workarounds while permanent fixes are developed. This systematic approach to problem resolution appeals to enterprises dealing with complex IT environments where the same underlying issues manifest across multiple incidents. ServiceNow ITSM strengths include: Comprehensive ITIL alignment with out-of-the-box processes that follow industry frameworks Robust reporting and dashboards for tracking SLA performance, backlog trends, and team productivity Deep integration capabilities connecting to virtually any enterprise application through APIs and pre-built connectors Enterprise audit trails maintaining detailed records of every action for compliance and governance requirements Multi-tenant architecture supporting complex organizational structures with separate service desks per business unit Service Catalog and Request Fulfillment The service catalog allows IT teams to publish standardized offerings that employees can request through self-service portals. Common catalog items include hardware requests, software installations, access provisioning, and password resets. ServiceNow's catalog strength lies in its ability to attach complex fulfillment workflows to seemingly simple requests. A laptop request might automatically trigger procurement approval, budget verification, asset tagging, software imaging, and delivery scheduling without IT staff manually coordinating each step. The limitation emerges when employees must leave their daily work environment to access this catalog. Even well-designed ServiceNow portals require employees to remember URLs, navigate unfamiliar interfaces, and translate their actual needs into ServiceNow's categorization structure. Unthread's automation builder addresses this friction by enabling IT teams to create fulfillment workflows that employees trigger directly from Slack. Similar approval chains and integrations can run from a simple Slack message, reducing the need for a separate portal visit while maintaining structured tracking and compliance. Analyzing ServiceNow's AI Platform and AI Control Tower for the Future ServiceNow has invested heavily in AI capabilities, positioning the Now Platform as an intelligent automation engine rather than just a ticketing system. The AI Control Tower provides visibility into AI usage across the platform, while predictive intelligence, virtual agents, and automated workflow recommendations represent the core AI feature set. Impact of AI on Service Delivery ServiceNow's virtual agent technology enables conversational interactions for common requests. Employees can chat with a virtual agent to reset passwords, check ticket status, or submit standard requests without involving human agents. The platform's predictive intelligence assigns priority, category, and assignment group based on ticket content, reducing manual triage work for IT teams. However, ServiceNow's AI capabilities require significant investment to deliver results. Organizations must: Build and maintain training data specific to their environment, terminology, and processes Configure conversation flows for each use case the virtual agent should handle Integrate knowledge sources that the AI can reference when generating responses Monitor and tune performance as language patterns and request types evolve Manage AI governance to ensure responses meet organizational standards This implementation overhead means many ServiceNow customers never fully activate the AI features they've purchased. The capabilities exist, but the configuration work to make them effective exceeds available IT resources. AI-Driven Operational Intelligence The AI Control Tower provides visibility into how AI is being used across ServiceNow modules, including adoption metrics, deflection rates, and recommendations for expanding AI usage. For organizations with mature ServiceNow deployments and dedicated platform teams, this centralized AI governance proves valuable. ServiceNow's AIOps capabilities extend into IT operations, using machine learning to correlate alerts, predict outages, and recommend remediation actions. These features target large enterprises with complex infrastructure where manual correlation of monitoring data is impractical. Unthread's agentic AI takes a different approach, delivering purpose-built AI agents that work immediately without extensive configuration. The system understands request intent using large language models, references knowledge base content, and drafts accurate responses before human handoff. Organizations can achieve substantial ticket deflection with platforms like Unthread, with purpose-built AI agents resolving routine requests without the same level of custom AI setup that ServiceNow implementations may require. The key difference lies in philosophy: ServiceNow provides AI building blocks that skilled administrators must assemble; Unthread provides AI agents that handle internal support workflows out of the box. ServiceNow's Competitive Landscape: Alternatives and Competitors ServiceNow competes across multiple categories, facing different competitors depending on the specific use case. For ITSM, Atlassian's Jira Service Management, Freshservice, and BMC Helix represent the primary alternatives. For HR service delivery, Workday and dedicated HR platforms compete for budget and attention. Key competitive dynamics in 2026 include: Jira Service Management appeals to development-centric organizations already using Atlassian products, offering tighter alignment with agile workflows and lower total cost for smaller IT teams Freshservice targets mid-market IT teams with faster implementation timelines and more accessible pricing than ServiceNow's enterprise model BMC Helix competes directly at the enterprise level with similar capabilities and complexity, often winning when organizations have existing BMC relationships Workday increasingly handles HR service delivery for organizations using Workday HCM, reducing ServiceNow's HR module opportunity The most significant competitive shift, however, comes from communication-native platforms that challenge the assumption that service management requires a separate system. Organizations running their operations in Slack or Microsoft Teams increasingly question why employees must visit portals when they could submit and track requests from their daily communication tools. Unthread's complete platform features represent this new competitive category. Rather than requiring employees to context-switch into ServiceNow, Unthread turns Slack channels into full internal help desks with structured ticketing, routing, and workflow automation. IT teams can designate a channel like #it-help as the single intake location for employee requests, with some ticket types remaining in-channel while others move to DMs or private flows for privacy reasons. This approach reduces training overhead, supports adoption, and reduces the time employees spend explaining their issues through form fields and category selections. The same information emerges naturally from conversational requests. Workflow Automation Software: ServiceNow's Strengths Across the Enterprise ServiceNow's Flow Designer and IntegrationHub enable organizations to build automated workflows that span multiple systems. The platform's strength lies in orchestrating complex, multi-step processes that touch numerous applications and require sophisticated conditional logic. Beyond IT: HR, Employee Service, and Operations Workflows ServiceNow's workflow capabilities extend well beyond IT. HR teams use the platform for employee onboarding workflows that coordinate actions across IT (provisioning accounts), facilities (assigning desks), security (badge access), and HR (benefits enrollment). A single onboarding request can trigger dozens of downstream tasks without manual coordination. Employee service workflows route internal requests based on employee attributes, priority, and team availability. Operations teams automate procurement approvals, vendor management, and contract renewals through ServiceNow workflows. ServiceNow workflow automation advantages include: Visual workflow designer allowing process owners to build automations without coding Pre-built integration connectors for common enterprise applications Conditional branching supporting complex decision logic based on request data Parallel execution running multiple workflow branches simultaneously Error handling with retry logic and exception management Approval chains supporting sequential, parallel, and ad-hoc approval patterns The Power of the Now Platform for Automation ServiceNow's platform approach means workflows can access any data within the system. An IT automation can reference HR data to verify employment status, check asset inventory, query the CMDB for configuration details, and update financial systems, all within a single workflow. This integration depth proves valuable for enterprises with complex cross-functional processes. When a single workflow must coordinate IT, HR, finance, and legal actions, ServiceNow's unified platform may provide broader orchestration than narrower point solutions. The trade-off emerges in administrative overhead. Building and maintaining these workflows requires ServiceNow expertise that many organizations struggle to develop internally. What looks straightforward in demos becomes complex when accounting for organizational edge cases, integration failures, and changing business requirements. Unthread's automation builder offers three creation methods that reduce this complexity: natural language descriptions that convert to working automations, visual drag-and-drop interfaces for workflow design, and custom code integrations for advanced logic. Teams can create automations using the approach that matches their technical comfort level, with pre-built integrations for platforms like Jira, Salesforce, ServiceNow itself, and Okta. For organizations that already use ServiceNow for enterprise processes, Unthread can complement the platform by handling conversational ticket intake and resolution in Slack while syncing to ServiceNow for complex workflows requiring its orchestration capabilities. A Look at ServiceNow's Developer Ecosystem and Certification Paths ServiceNow has built a substantial developer community and certification program that supports both the platform's adoption and career paths for technical professionals. The ServiceNow Developer Program provides free personal developer instances, training resources, and documentation for building on the platform. Key elements of the ServiceNow developer ecosystem: Developer instances providing free access to full ServiceNow environments for learning and experimentation ServiceNow Studio offering an integrated development environment for building applications Flow Designer enabling low-code automation development Scripting capabilities using JavaScript and GlideRecord APIs for custom functionality App Store marketplace hosting applications from partners and the community The certification program spans multiple tracks, including System Administrator, Application Developer, Implementation Specialist, and specialized certifications for modules like ITSM, HRSD, and CSM. These certifications have become valuable career credentials, with certified ServiceNow professionals commanding premium salaries in the enterprise IT market. This ecosystem represents both a strength and a lock-in mechanism. Organizations benefit from available talent and learning resources, but the specialized skills required mean switching costs increase as ServiceNow expertise becomes embedded in IT teams. ServiceNow's Portal and User Experience: A Critical Assessment ServiceNow's Employee Center and Service Portal represent the platform's approach to self-service. These portals allow organizations to present service catalog items, knowledge articles, and ticket status through branded web interfaces that employees access separately from their daily work tools. Streamlining Self-Service with Modern Portals The Employee Center consolidates IT, HR, and other internal services into a unified experience. Employees can submit requests, browse knowledge articles, check ticket status, and access frequently used resources from a single location. The interface supports personalization based on employee attributes, showing relevant content and services based on department, location, and role. ServiceNow has invested in improving portal usability, with responsive designs that work across devices and search capabilities that help employees find relevant content. The latest versions include conversational interfaces where employees can describe their needs in natural language rather than browsing categories. Enhancing Engagement through the Employee Center Despite these improvements, portal-based self-service faces an inherent adoption challenge. Employees must remember to visit the portal, navigate to the correct area, and translate their needs into the portal's structure. No matter how well-designed, this approach adds friction compared to requesting help in the communication tools employees already use throughout their workday. Usage data consistently shows that portal-based service management experiences low adoption rates outside mandatory processes. Employees default to email, Slack messages to IT colleagues, or stopping by IT desks rather than using self-service portals that require additional effort. Unthread's omni-channel intake offers an alternative approach, bringing Slack messages, DMs, email, and portal-style requests into one internal support workflow. Teams can meet employees where they already work, with all channels unified in a single inbox and ticket workflows managed from Slack. For HR teams specifically, Unthread enables private ticketing for sensitive requests. Employees can submit inquiries about payroll, parental leave, benefits, or policy questions without leaving Slack, with privacy controls ensuring sensitive conversations stay confidential while maintaining the structured ticketing that HR teams need for tracking and compliance. Considering ServiceNow Careers and Its Impact on IT Service Management Jobs ServiceNow expertise has become a distinct career path within IT, with roles ranging from administrators managing day-to-day operations to architects designing enterprise implementations. The platform's complexity creates sustained demand for skilled professionals who understand both the technical capabilities and business process implications. Common ServiceNow career paths include: ServiceNow Administrator managing platform configuration, user accounts, and routine maintenance ServiceNow Developer building custom applications, integrations, and automations Implementation Specialist configuring modules for initial deployment or expansion Solution Architect designing ServiceNow strategies that align with business requirements Business Analyst translating business needs into ServiceNow requirements Technical Consultant advising organizations on ServiceNow best practices and optimization The job market for ServiceNow professionals remains strong in 2026, particularly for those with implementation experience and current certifications. Organizations continue to invest in ServiceNow platforms and need talent to maintain and expand their deployments. However, this specialization creates career concentration risk. Skills developed for ServiceNow don't always transfer directly to other platforms, and organizations reducing their ServiceNow footprint may find their expertise less marketable than broader IT service management or workflow automation skills. ServiceNow Stock and Financial Outlook: Investment Health in 2026 ServiceNow (NYSE: NOW) has maintained its position as a leading enterprise SaaS company, with market capitalization and revenue growth that reflects continued enterprise adoption. The company's financial performance demonstrates the durability of its business model, with high customer retention rates and expanding contract values as existing customers add modules. Key Financial Indicators ServiceNow's subscription-based revenue model provides predictable recurring revenue that investors value highly. The company has demonstrated consistent growth through both new customer acquisition and expansion within existing accounts. Contract value increases as organizations deploy additional ServiceNow modules beyond their initial ITSM implementations. The platform's stickiness contributes to strong net retention rates. Once organizations deploy ServiceNow and build processes around it, switching costs make migration to alternatives expensive and risky. This retention dynamic supports premium valuations typical of enterprise SaaS leaders. Strategic Growth Initiatives ServiceNow's growth strategy centers on platform expansion beyond traditional ITSM. The company has invested in industry-specific solutions for telecommunications, financial services, healthcare, and government sectors. These vertical solutions combine ServiceNow's platform capabilities with pre-built workflows and integrations tailored to industry requirements. AI represents a major strategic focus, with the company positioning its platform as the foundation for enterprise AI initiatives. ServiceNow's argument to investors and customers emphasizes that AI capabilities are most valuable when connected to structured workflow data that the Now Platform provides. For organizations evaluating ServiceNow, the company's financial stability suggests continued product investment and long-term viability. However, financial success doesn't automatically translate to the best fit for every organization's internal support needs. Enterprise Software Trends: Where ServiceNow Stands in 2026 ServiceNow's market position reflects broader enterprise software trends that shape how organizations think about internal service delivery. Understanding these trends helps evaluate where ServiceNow fits and where alternatives may better serve specific needs. The Rise of Hyperautomation Hyperautomation describes the trend toward automating every possible business process through combinations of workflow automation, AI, and robotic process automation. ServiceNow has positioned itself as a hyperautomation platform, offering the tools organizations need to automate increasingly complex processes. The platform's strength in this context lies in its ability to serve as a system of action that coordinates automation across enterprise applications. When automation requires orchestrating multiple systems, maintaining audit trails, and handling exceptions, ServiceNow's platform approach may provide broader orchestration than standalone automation tools. Unthread's agentic AI represents a different approach to automation, one focused specifically on internal support workflows where the goal is resolving employee requests faster rather than orchestrating enterprise-wide processes. The platform's AI agents handle ticket deflection, response generation, and routine request fulfillment directly in Slack, delivering automation value without the implementation complexity that enterprise hyperautomation initiatives typically require. The Shift to Experience-Centric Platforms Employee experience has become a strategic priority for enterprises, with organizations recognizing that internal services shape productivity, satisfaction, and retention. This shift favors platforms that minimize friction over those that optimize for IT department efficiency at employees' expense. ServiceNow has responded with Employee Center investments aimed at consolidating employee services into more usable interfaces. However, the fundamental architecture, where employees must visit a separate system to request help, creates inherent friction that portal improvements cannot fully address. Unthread's native Slack integration reduces this friction by keeping requests inside Slack. Employees request help by sending a message in a Slack channel or DM. They receive updates in Slack. They never leave the application where they already spend their workday. This zero context-switching approach directly addresses the employee experience imperative that enterprise software trends emphasize. For organizations prioritizing employee experience alongside IT operational requirements, the choice increasingly comes down to whether ServiceNow's enterprise capabilities justify the friction it creates, or whether Slack-native alternatives can meet operational requirements while delivering superior employee experiences. Honest Pros and Cons of ServiceNow in 2026 After examining ServiceNow's capabilities, competitive position, and market context, the honest assessment requires acknowledging both genuine strengths and real limitations. ServiceNow Pros: Enterprise scalability supporting the largest organizations with complex requirements Comprehensive functionality spanning ITSM, HR, operations, security, and custom applications Mature ITIL processes providing out-of-the-box alignment with industry frameworks Deep integration capabilities connecting to virtually any enterprise application Robust compliance and audit features meeting regulatory requirements across industries Strong talent ecosystem with available skills and learning resources Financial stability ensuring continued product investment and long-term viability ServiceNow Cons: High total cost of ownership including licensing, implementation, and ongoing administration Extended implementation timelines for larger or more complex deployments Administrative complexity demanding specialized skills for configuration and maintenance Employee adoption challenges as portal-based interfaces create friction versus daily work tools AI setup overhead requiring significant configuration to deliver promised automation benefits Vendor lock-in risk as specialized expertise and process dependencies increase switching costs Over-engineering for simpler needs when full enterprise capabilities exceed actual requirements The right choice depends on organizational context. Enterprises with complex cross-functional workflows, large IT budgets, and dedicated platform teams can extract significant value from ServiceNow's comprehensive capabilities. Mid-market organizations, teams already operating in Slack, and departments seeking faster time-to-value may find that modern alternatives deliver better outcomes with lower overhead. Frequently Asked Questions What types of organizations benefit most from ServiceNow versus Slack-native alternatives? ServiceNow delivers the strongest value for large enterprises with complex, cross-functional workflows that span multiple departments and systems. Organizations with dedicated ServiceNow administrators, existing platform investments, and processes requiring ITIL-aligned change management benefit from the platform's comprehensive capabilities. Conversely, smaller organizations, teams already collaborating in Slack, and departments prioritizing fast deployment over enterprise orchestration may find Slack-native solutions easier to adopt. The key evaluation criteria include available administrative resources, integration complexity, employee experience priorities, and timeline requirements. Organizations using Slack as their primary collaboration tool should seriously evaluate whether a separate ticketing portal adds value or just friction. How does ServiceNow's pricing compare to alternatives for internal IT and HR support? ServiceNow uses enterprise pricing models that vary based on modules, user counts, and negotiated terms, making direct comparisons difficult. However, total cost of ownership extends well beyond licensing to include implementation services (often requiring specialized consultants), ongoing administration (typically requiring one or more dedicated staff), customization and integration development, and training for both administrators and end users. Many organizations report that implementation costs exceed first-year licensing, with ongoing administration representing a significant recurring expense. Slack-native alternatives like Unthread offer more predictable pricing starting at $50 per agent monthly with faster implementation timelines and lower administrative overhead. Organizations should calculate total cost over three to five years, including internal staff time, rather than comparing license costs alone. Can ServiceNow integrate with Slack for a hybrid approach to internal support? ServiceNow offers Slack integration through its IntegrationHub, allowing notifications, ticket creation, and basic interactions from Slack. However, this integration represents ServiceNow extending into Slack rather than native Slack functionality. Users still interact with ServiceNow's data structures, terminology, and workflow constraints, just through a Slack interface. The experience differs significantly from purpose-built Slack ticketing where the conversation itself becomes the ticket. Organizations sometimes deploy both platforms, using Slack-native solutions for frontline employee requests and ServiceNow for complex workflows requiring enterprise orchestration. This hybrid approach can deliver the best of both approaches if carefully architected to avoid duplicate data entry and process confusion. What should organizations consider before committing to a multi-year ServiceNow contract? Before signing extended ServiceNow agreements, organizations should conduct realistic assessments of implementation timelines based on similar organizations rather than vendor estimates, available internal resources for ongoing administration and optimization, actual employee adoption rates for existing self-service initiatives, specific use cases that require ServiceNow's enterprise capabilities versus those that simpler tools could address, and total cost projections including internal staff time, consulting support, and training. Running a proof of concept with a specific department or use case before enterprise commitment helps validate assumptions. Organizations should also evaluate whether their requirements might be better served by best-of-breed solutions for specific functions rather than a single platform approach that optimizes for IT department consolidation over employee experience. How do ServiceNow's AI capabilities compare to purpose-built AI agents for internal support? ServiceNow's AI capabilities are extensive but require significant configuration to deliver results. Organizations must build training data, configure conversation flows, integrate knowledge sources, and continuously tune performance. The platform's AI serves as building blocks that skilled administrators assemble rather than ready-to-use solutions. Purpose-built AI agents like those in Unthread take a different approach, delivering immediate value through pre-trained models that understand internal support request patterns. Organizations using purpose-built AI agents can achieve meaningful automatic resolution without the same level of custom AI setup that ServiceNow implementations may require. The choice depends on whether your organization has the resources and expertise to build custom AI solutions on ServiceNow's platform or prefers AI that works out of the box for common internal support scenarios

title: Kelly appoints Alan Stukalsky as Chief Product and Technology Officer
summary: Alan Stukalsky joins Kelly as chief product and technology officer, overseeing the company's product strategy, technology capabilities, and digital innovation efforts.
body_text: Industry veteran brings more than 25 years of technology and digital leadership to newly created role TROY, Mich. (July 6, 2026) – Kelly (Nasdaq: KELYA, KELYB), a global workforce strategy and solutions provider, has appointed Alan Stukalsky as chief product and technology officer, effective July 13. Stukalsky joins the Kelly senior leadership team, reporting to CEO Chris Layden, and will be responsible for overseeing the company's product strategy, technology capabilities, and digital innovation efforts across its portfolio of specialty businesses. "The workforce solutions industry is at an inflection point. Companies who successfully embed AI into their operations to better serve clients and candidates are going to pull away from the field," Layden said. "That work is already underway at Kelly. Alan will scale it, drive operational excellence across the enterprise, and accelerate the pace at which we’re launching products that will help clients build tech-enabled workforces. He’s done it before and we’re excited to see the impact he’ll bring." Stukalsky brings more than 25 years of technology leadership and digital transformation experience to the newly created role. Throughout his career, he has led large-scale modernization efforts, enterprise platform transformations, cloud migrations, AI-enabled innovation, and the development of new digital business models. He is widely recognized for aligning technology, product, and business strategy to create industry-leading talent solutions and deliver measurable outcomes for customers, employees, and shareholders. Most recently, Stukalsky served as chief digital and information officer at LHH, part of the Adecco Group. Prior to LHH, Stukalsky spent more than 16 years at Randstad, holding dual executive roles as chief digital officer and chief information officer for North America. "This is an exciting time to join Kelly. The company is investing in the technology and products that will define how it competes in an AI-driven market," Stukalsky said. "I'm passionate about making it easier for clients and candidates to work with us, embedding AI into the fabric of how we operate, and ensuring the people we place are equipped with the tools they need to succeed. I look forward to partnering with the talented Kelly team to build on a strong foundation and accelerate growth." Stukalsky is a passionate advocate for inspiring future STEM professionals and active with Junior Achievement, Georgia State University’s CIS program, and STE(A)M Truck. He has served on numerous industry and community boards and has been recognized as Georgia CIO of the Year for Large Enterprises. He holds a Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering from Georgia Tech and a Bachelor of Science in Mathematics from Emory University. About Kelly® Kelly Services, Inc. (Nasdaq: KELYA, KELYB) helps companies recruit and manage skilled workers and helps job seekers find great work. Since inventing the staffing industry in 1946, we have become experts in the many industries and local and global markets we serve. With a network of suppliers and partners around the world, we connect approximately 375,000 people with work every year. title: The National Coalition of Certification Centers and 3M award national scholarships to skilled trades students nationwide
summary: The National Coalition of Certification Centers (NC3), in partnership with 3M’s Safety and Industrial business, announced the 2026 recipients of the Skilled Trades – 3M Transformational...
body_text: The National Coalition of Certification Centers ( NC3 ), in partnership with 3M’s Safety and Industrial business, announced the 2026 recipients of the Skilled Trades – 3M Transformational Scholarship. This annual scholarship helps empower students pursuing technical and skilled trades careers by providing essential financial support and helping expand access to opportunities in communities across the country. Supporting the next generation of skilled trades professionals This year, 52 students from across the United States were each awarded $1,000 scholarships during NC3’s annual National Career and Technical Education Letter of Intent Signing Day . Modeled after NCAA’s National Signing Day, this celebration honors and recognizes students as they formally commit to career and technical education pathways—affirming the value, dignity, and promise of skilled trades professions. “Supporting this next generation of skilled trades professionals is a true privilege,” said Michael Stroik, Vice President, 3M Community Impact. “These students are choosing careers that shape the infrastructure, safety, and innovation of our world. By investing in a diverse and talented workforce, we are helping build stronger communities and a stronger future for all.” A national celebration of career and technical education This year, nearly 90 NC3 Signing Day ceremonies united students, families, educators, and industry partners nationwide. These events showcased the pride and enthusiasm surrounding career and technical education, highlighting student pathways in manufacturing, transportation, energy, construction, and other high‑demand fields that help keep our economy moving. Expanding access and opportunity The Skilled Trades – 3M Transformational Scholarship represents more than financial assistance. It opens doors for students, allowing them to focus on building the hands‑on skills and industry-recognized certifications that will set them apart in today’s workforce. Findings from a Harris Poll conducted in 2025 show that sponsoring hands-on skilled trades programs in schools and providing scholarships or training funds for trade education rank among the most impactful ways companies can support skilled tradespeople in their communities. “NC3 National Signing Day shines a spotlight on the students who will become tomorrow’s leaders in the skilled trades,” said Roger Tadajewski, NC3 Executive Director . “Our partnership with 3M reflects our shared commitment to supporting students, strengthening career pathways, and ensuring that today’s learners become the well‑trained professionals our industries depend on.” A shared commitment to workforce development As demand for skilled labor continues to grow nationwide, programs like the Skilled Trades – 3M Transformational Scholarship help prepare students to thrive in evolving, high-growth industries. 3M and NC3 remain dedicated to investing in technical education, supporting workforce innovation, and empowering students to reach their full potential. To learn more about NC3 National Signing Day and view the recipients of the Skilled Trades – 3M Transformational Scholarship, please visit www.nc3.net/signingday .

title: U.S. GoldMining Identifies New Au-Cu Porphyry Targets from 2025 Exploration Program at the Whistler Gold-Copper Project, Alaska
summary: U.S. GoldMining Inc. is an exploration and development company focused on advancing the 100% owned Whistler Gold-Copper Project, Alaska
body_text: U.S. GoldMining Identifies New Au-Cu Porphyry Targets from 2025 Exploration Program at the Whistler Gold-Copper Project, Alaska Share: Download PDF: Anchorage, Alaska – January 20, 2026 – U.S. GoldMining Inc. (NASDAQ: USGO) (“ U.S. GoldMining ” or the “ Company ”) is pleased to announce the initial results of the 2025 exploration program at its 100% owned Whistler Gold-Copper Project (the " Whistler Project " or " Project "). The 2025 exploration program focused on targeting potential resource growth through developing new drill targets at the Whistler Orbit and Muddy Creek prospect areas; this release compiles the results from the scout drilling program completed over the Whistler Orbit. 2025 Whistler Orbit Exploration Results: Four new high priority target areas identified from basal till and/or top of bedrock gold-copper geochemistry, combined with geological mapping of porphyry distribution and geophysical surveys (magnetics ± IP chargeability), suggestive of potential for the future discovery of new bedrock porphyry gold-copper mineralization: Whistler extensions – new zones of copper anomalism in both basal till and top of bedrock sampling located immediately east of the currently delineated Whistler deposit. Mammoth & Snow Ridge – two new large gold ± copper anomalies located 2-3 kilometers north of the Whistler deposit comprised of broad intense gold anomalies in tills and bedrock. Raintree area – widespread gold ± copper anomalism indicative of wingspan extensions immediately adjacent to the existing Raintree deposit and throughout the broader target area. Hotfoot – emerging new target defined by an intense bedrock gold anomaly associated with a large ‘Whistler look-alike’ magnetic anomaly 1 kilometer south of Raintree deposit. The highest priority targets are now being prepared for follow-up infill and expansion scout drilling, followed by deeper diamond core drilling, projected to commence in summer 2026. The Company continues to advance its previously announced initial assessment study (" PEA ") for the Project (see news release dated June 9, 2025). Tim Smith, Chief Executive Officer of U.S. GoldMining, commented: “We are pleased with the outcome of the scout drilling program completed over the Whistler Orbit area in 2025, which provided further indication of the potential for discovery of new Au-Cu porphyry deposits. The objective of the 2025 summer program was to follow up on the over 25 individual geophysical intrusive targets previously identified from magnetic inversion modelling, by systematically collecting geochemical data across the Whistler-Raintree porphyry cluster to provide an additional vector to defining high priority drill targets. Several zones of strongly anomalous Au & Cu in basal till and top of bedrock samples, in conjunction with lithologic mapping and the existing geophysical data, provide compelling evidence in support of conducting deeper systematic core drilling to test for new discoveries of bedrock hosted economic Au-Cu mineralization, which is currently being planned for the upcoming 2026 field season. Additional pending exploration results for the Muddy Creek program, also completed during the 2025 field season, will be provided in due course as analysis and interpretation is completed. The Whistler PEA is progressing, and the Company is currently aiming to release results before the end of Q1 2026. We believe that the combination of gold, copper and silver hitting all-time high commodity prices over recent months, the existing large gold-copper-silver mineral resource and district-scale exploration potential and the project’s location in one of America's most prospective and mining-friendly jurisdictions, Alaska, marks a potential inflection point for the Company over the coming year. We look forward to providing further updates on the Whistler Project, including our plans for ongoing exploration and further mine scoping studies throughout the year ahead.” Figure 1 The Whistler Project, containing three gold ± copper ± silver mineral systems: Whistler – Raintree , which contains the currently delineated Whistler and Raintree deposits; Island Mountain which contains the namesake gold deposit and several additional undrilled targets; and Muddy Creek which holds potential for discovery of an intrusive related gold system. 2025 Whistler Exploration Program Details The Company completed a scout drilling program (the “ Program ”) in August-October 2025, of 169 shallow drillholes (ranging from 3m to 8m hole depth) over the Whistler–Raintree mineral system, or ‘Whistler Orbit’ – see Figure 1 . The Whistler Orbit represents a classic porphyry cluster over an area of approximately 7.5 km by 4.5 km comprising multiple porphyry targets surrounding the existing Whistler and Raintree gold-copper porphyry deposits. The Program had the objective of adding geochemical pathfinder vectors to build upon geophysical modelling which indicates over 25 individual potential porphyry intrusive bodies located beneath glacial till cover in the Whistler Orbit. Figure 2 Top: Geochemical response in basal till samples (left: gold; right: copper). Bottom: Geochemical response in top of bedrock samples (left: gold; right: copper). The scout drilling program was conducted by SLR Consulting (Canada) Ltd. (" SLR "), using a helicopter portable ‘Shock Auger’ drilling system, which is designed to penetrate glacial till deposits to collect a sample at the base of glacial deposits (the overburden-bedrock interface). Where possible, a top-of-bedrock rock chip sample is also collected from the underlying bedrock. A pattern of evenly spaced scout drillholes was completed over exploration areas interpreted from surficial geological mapping to have shallow glacial till cover, comprised of unconsolidated gravel, sand and clay which overlies (‘covers’) the bedrock which is prospective for porphyry Au-Cu mineralization. The drill hole pattern was designed on a perpendicular alignment to the ancient glacial ice-flow direction, with the objective of being able to track basal-till anomalies in the ‘up ice’ direction towards a possible bedrock source. Two exploration areas were targeted with contiguous grids of evenly spaced scout drill holes: the Whistler-Raintree area, and the Mammoth exploration area north of Portage Creek. The objective of the Program was to collect geochemical data to vector towards potential undetected porphyry Au-Cu mineralization beneath the till cover, which averages 2-10 meters in thickness over 80% of the Whistler Orbit area. The Company has previously defined over 25 individual potential exploration targets within the Whistler Orbit (see news release dated May 27, 2025), each comprising a geophysical signature similar to the known Whistler deposit. The Program was successful in collecting a basal till sample in all 169 drill holes and collected top of bedrock chips in 63% of the holes drilled, intersecting multiple occurrences of previously unmapped porphyry intrusive rocks beneath till cover. Porphyry-related geochemical anomalism is defined via a statistical process, to determine relative enrichment of Au, Cu and related pathfinder elements, above naturally occurring ‘background’ levels. Statistical thresholds for moderate, high, and intense geochemical anomalism were established as Robust Z-Score values of 1, 2, and 3 respectively. Four principle Au ± Cu target areas are emerging within the Whistler Orbit area: Whistler extensions, Raintree extensions, Mammoth, and Hotfoot (see Figure 2 ). Whistler wingspan target area: Scout drilling adjacent to the Whistler deposit targeted Induced Polarity (" IP ") chargeability anomalies in bedrock beneath till cover located north and east of the drill delineated mineral resources (see news release dated October 7, 2024). Drilling discovered a strong to intense copper anomaly in basal till with an associated moderately anomalous bedrock response at the ‘Coronet’ target area, located immediately east of the Whistler deposit. This new geochemical anomaly is suggestive of the potential for additional wingspan expansion of the known Whistler deposit mineralization. Mammoth & Snow Ridge target area: The Mammoth area of exploration interest, located 2 kilometers north of the Whistler deposit, was first detected from 2024 top-of-till geochemistry results, which showed anomalous gold values overlying a large magnetic-high feature, which in 3D inversion modelling demonstrates similar geometry to the Whistler host porphyry diorite stock i.e. a ‘Whistler look-alike’ magnetic anomaly. The Program comprised a broad wide-spaced scout drill grid over the magnetic anomaly and additional exploratory holes ‘up-ice’ of the anomalous top-of-till values in the ‘Snow Ridge’ area. Strong to intensely anomalous gold values were reported in both tills and top of bedrock samples over the Mammoth East & West areas. Additionally, an emerging zone of moderate to intensely anomalous gold and moderate to strong copper, in both tills and bedrock, was identified at the Snow Ridge area located 1 kilometer northwest of Mammoth. Both prospect areas require further exploration to improve delineation of the new targets, followed by deeper diamond core drilling. Raintree target area: The Raintree area of exploration interest aimed to explore surface expressions adjacent to the Raintree West deposit, including chargeability features to the north and south of the deposit, and historically under-drilled parts of the Raintree North and Raintree East prospects. The program identified widespread copper and gold anomalies throughout the broad target area. Anomalous values overlying and surrounding the delineated Raintree deposit helps to confirm the effectiveness of the exploration methodology and in addition suggests potential for additional wingspan extensions. Broad zones of strong to intense gold in tills and bedrock, supported by moderate copper values in basal till over the Raintree North and East targets further supports additional exploration in these areas which have only been lightly drilled historically with diamond core. Hotfoot target area: Scout drilling was extended to the southwest of the Raintree target area to explore the emerging ‘Hotfoot’ target area, an underexplored magnetic feature with similar geometry (from 3D inversion modelling) to the Whistler deposit and Mammoth magnetic anomalies. The drilling returned anomalous gold-in-till down-ice of the Hotfoot target, and a large intense gold-in-bedrock anomaly directly overlying high gold values previously reported in deep diamond core drilling (WH24-05: 138.00 m at 0.99 g/t AuEq, comprised of 0.89 g/t Au, 0.05 % Cu and 17.57 g/t Ag, plus 0.44% Pb and 0.95% Zn, from 635.0 m downhole; see news release February 10, 2025), which is interpreted to represent ‘D-style’ porphyry veins potentially associated with an as yet unidentified nearby source porphyry. Additional infill and step out scout drilling will need to be conducted over the Hotfoot target area to better refine this target. Overall, the 2025 scout drilling program over the Whistler Orbit returned multiple zones of highly anomalous gold ± copper in both basal till and top of bedrock sampling. These anomalies are frequently coincident with newly mapped porphyry lithologies beneath the till cover, logged from top of bedrock drill chips. Combined with the geophysical datasets, including 3D magnetic inversion modelling of porphyry stocks and dykes, and/or IP chargeability which detects potential phyllic (quartz-sericite-pyrite) alteration zones, the scout drill method provides a robust basis for the Company to identify and prioritize diamond core drill targets for the upcoming 2026 summer field season. Additional information on the future planned diamond core drilling program and budget will be released in the coming months. Technical Information For further information regarding the Project and the mineral resource estimates referenced herein, refer to the technical report summary titled “S-K 1300 Technical Report Summary Initial Assessment for the Whistler Project, South Central Alaska” with an effective date of September 12, 2024, and the technical report titled “NI 43-101 2024 Updated Mineral Resource Estimate for the Whistler Project, South Central Alaska” with an effective date of September 12, 2024, available under the Company’s respective profiles at www.sec.gov and www.sedarplus.ca . Tim Smith, P.Geo., Chief Executive Officer of U.S. GoldMining, has supervised the preparation of this news release and has reviewed and approved the scientific and technical information contained herein. Mr. Smith is a "qualified person" as defined in Canadian National Instrument 43-101 – Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects. About U.S. GoldMining Inc. U.S. GoldMining Inc. is an exploration and development company focused on advancing the 100% owned Whistler Gold-Copper Project, located 105 miles (170 kilometers) northwest of Anchorage, Alaska, U.S.A. The Whistler Project consists of several gold-copper porphyry deposits and exploration targets within a large regional land package entirely on State of Alaska Mining claims totaling approximately 53,700 acres (217.5 square kilometers). The Whistler Project Mineral Resource Estimate comprises 294 Mt at 0.68 g/t AuEq for 6.48 Moz AuEq Indicated, plus 198 Mt at 0.65 g/t AuEq for 4.16 Moz AuEq Inferred. Visit www.usgoldmining.us for more information, including high resolution figures. For additional information, please contact: U.S. GoldMining Inc. title: What the EPA water infrastructure funding push means for your field operations
summary: Learn how expedited water infrastructure funding can affect environmental consulting firms and project timelines.
body_text: The EPA is speeding up delivery of several major water infrastructure funding programs, including the Drinking Water and Clean Water State Revolving Funds, the WIFIA loan program, and the Emerging Contaminants grant. Together, these programs direct federal investment toward water systems and projects that protect water quality and public health. Faster funding means a faster-arriving wave of permitting, inspection, and reporting work for the environmental consulting firms that support water utility clients. Here’s what that shift means for field teams, and why documentation readiness decides which firms absorb it smoothly. Key insights Accelerated EPA funding delivery compresses compliance schedules for water infrastructure projects without reducing mandatory regulatory requirements. The EPA’s advance notice gives consulting firms a critical window to modernize field operations before project volumes surge. State-by-state reporting variations create severe compliance challenges for expanding firms that rely on rigid field software. Fulcrum provides the necessary agility through no-code state template customization, customizable regulatory logic, and offline GIS integration. Documentation readiness ultimately determines whether a firm can absorb incoming project volume seamlessly or face costly operational bottlenecks. On July 9, 2026, the EPA convened its first roundtable on water infrastructure funding delivery, with a clear focus on speed: getting appropriated dollars moving faster than usual. The goal was to close the gap between when Congress appropriates funding and when it reaches projects on the ground. The agenda covered several of the federal government’s largest water infrastructure funding programs, together with the financing pipeline behind most of the nation’s drinking water, wastewater, and stormwater management projects . Across the water sector , those dollars support systems serving both large utilities and small communities. Environmental consulting firms that support water utility clients work inside that same pipeline. On the surface, the EPA’s push to speed up water infrastructure funding is a policy story. Underneath, for environmental consulting firms serving utility clients, it is a workload story. Permitting, inspection, and reporting volume tied to SRF, WIFIA, and Emerging Contaminants grants is about to increase, no matter how ready a firm’s documentation happens to be. Funding programs behind the EPA’s push for faster delivery The EPA’s July 9 roundtable focused on programs designed to speed water infrastructure delivery. These included the Drinking Water and Clean Water State Revolving Funds , or DWSRF and CWSRF, the two largest financing vehicles for utility work. The roundtable also covered the Water Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act loan program, which finances larger regional projects through direct federal loans. The roundtable also addressed the Emerging Contaminants in Small and Disadvantaged Communities grant program, one of several water infrastructure grants that fund PFAS remediation work in small, underserved communities. The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA), also known as the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law , is a major source of this federal investment. EPA’s IIJA implementation strategy directs $43 billion through the SRF programs to help address local water quality and public health challenges. That funding includes dedicated support for lead service line replacement and emerging contaminants. All of these programs already existed before the roundtable. What changed is the EPA’s commitment to closing the appropriation-to-delivery gap for each one. For firms that already navigate the SRF loan program and WIFIA paperwork, the practical effect comes down to timing. Money moves through the pipeline more quickly than usual, and fieldwork follows close behind, on a tighter schedule. What accelerated water infrastructure funding means for your workload Faster funding delivery pushes every permitting review, inspection cycle, and regulatory report onto a shorter timeline. A drinking water state revolving fund loan that closes three months sooner still leaves the same compliance calendar to satisfy, just on a tighter clock. Every SRF-funded or WIFIA-funded project carries the same list of requir e ments : site inspections, chain-of-custody documentation, monitoring reports, and whatever paperwork the issuing state demands. None of that shrinks because the money arrived faster. Depending on the program, that scheduling pressure can reach water infrastructure improvement work involving lead service lines, sewer projects, and stormwater infrastructure. Projects designed for climate change resilience can add another layer of site-condition, inspection, and reporting requirements. Every prior round of funding growth in this sector has driven the same rise in project counts and compliance documentation. A firm handling a handful of SRF-funded projects today could be juggling many more within a year or two, once the funding lands. What sets this cycle apart is the advance notice. The EPA telegraphed its intent to speed delivery before funding started moving, giving firms time to prepare their field operations for higher project volume. However, advance notice only helps when existing workflows can scale. In practice, readiness comes down to what an environmental field data collection platform can already do: standardize inspections, adapt forms to state requirements, validate field records, and keep work moving without a reliable connection. Where Fulcrum’s environmental field data collection tools fit Advance notice becomes useful once a firm’s tools already handle a few specific things: adapting to state paperwork on the fly, building compliance logic into forms, and keeping data usable without a live connection. State-specific SRF reporting requirements SRF programs are federally funded but run separately by each state , each with its own field-level reporting requirements for water systems and their project teams. Federal funding meets local bureaucracy, creating a messy patchwork of compliance standards across state lines. A stormwater inspection form built for Ohio gets rejected in Texas. A Pennsylvania monitoring template requires a complete rebuild before working in Georgia. Every state protects its own standards, forcing consulting firms to adapt constantly. Expanding into new territories quickly creates operational chaos under tight funding deadlines. Traditional software forces project teams to wait on custom code or IT tickets for minor template tweaks. Fulcrum removes that bottleneck: project managers configure state-specific templates themselves, without waiting on a ticket queue . Field teams stay moving while compliance paperwork stays current. Real-world example: Environmental consulting firm DIEHLUX eliminated form-building delays during multi-state expansion. [ Read the customer story ] Regulatory reporting depth Environmental compliance work needs more than a basic inspection checklist . Chain-of-custody tracking, contaminant threshold logic, and state-specific reporting fields go beyond a photo and a GPS pin. A generic data collection platform can capture the basics. But proving a sample’s custody chain or flagging a threshold breach requires logic inside the form. Solutions without that native depth patch the gaps with spreadsheets and manual cross-referencing. Fulcrum’s customizable form creation lets a firm build chain-of-custody tracking or threshold-based flagging into a template, so a reading that falls outside an acceptable range gets flagged the moment it’s recorded. A project manager configuring a new SRF-funded engagement can set that logic up once and reuse it across future work. Finally, Fulcrum’s acquisition of environmental consulting software platform Wildnote brought its team’s environmental domain expertise fully into the company. GIS sync and offline capture Environmental consulting firms already rely on GIS platforms like Esri ArcGIS for mapping and spatial analysis, but getting field data into that system reliably is its own challenge. SRF- and WIFIA-funded work often happens at rural treatment plants and remote pipeline segments with unreliable cell coverage. Data collected offline in those conditions usually means manual re-entry once a crew is back in range, adding delay and room for error. That re-entry step is exactly what Fulcrum removes. Fulcrum syncs field records directly into GIS platforms, including Esri’s ArcGIS environment, and keeps them fully usable offline. A crew working a remote site without signal keeps collecting data, since everything syncs automatically once a connection returns. The office-based GIS team gets that same data without ever visiting the site. Why documentation readiness decides who absorbs this surge The policy story ended at the roundtable. The workload story is only getting started for firms serving water utility clients. SRF, WIFIA, and Emerging Contaminants volume is heading their way, ready or not. Firms already running standardized workflows will absorb that volume without adding headcount. They will not need to scramble to build new state-specific forms under deadline pressure. Everyone else will face the same crunch, just at a larger scale. The outcome comes down less to talent than to how early a firm started preparing. The gap between a prepared firm and an unprepared one only grows as funding moves through the pipeline. Learn more: Check out our webinar, Designing environmental field workflows for constant change , for more on regulatory shifts that could compound this funding-driven surge.

body_text: Press Release SCHMID Group Secures Repeat Order Exceeding EUR 37 Million for Advanced HDI-ML and mSAP Equipment Freudenstadt, Germany, July 7, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) — SCHMID Group (NASDAQ: SHMD) has received a repeat order exceeding EUR 37 million from a leading Chinese customer for advanced HDI-ML and mSAP production equipment . The equipment supports the customer’s next capacity expansion for next-generation AI server boards and optical module applications and follows the successful completion of the first phase supplied by SCHMID in 2025. The project further confirms SCHMID’s strong position as a leading equipment partner for advanced wet process solutions in mSAP, HDI and high-end interconnect manufacturing. AI infrastructure, high-speed networking and optical communication are driving the need for finer structures, higher signal integrity, better yield and reliable high-volume production. The ordered equipment will be used for the customer’s next capacity expansion in mSAP production. These processes enable finer line/space structures, higher routing density and improved electrical performance — key requirements for advanced AI server boards and optical module platforms used in modern data centers. SCHMID already supplied key equipment for the first phase of the customer’s capacity expansion last year. Given strong performance, high uptime, stable processes and excellent production reliability with our InfinityLine H+ and InfinityLine V+ platforms, this major Chinese customer has now selected SCHMID again for the next expansion step. SCHMID continues to benefit from the accelerating investment cycle in AI-related electronics manufacturing. We see strong momentum in advanced substrate, HDI and mSAP applications. Order intake in the six months ended June 30, 2026 reached EUR 44.3 million, excluding this order (with this order, order intake since January 1, 2026 amounted to EUR 81.7 million). Following the recent acceleration in order intake, the Company is currently reviewing an upward revision of its guidance on order intake. The Company is finalizing its updated full year 2026 order guidance and outlook and expects to communicate a revised quantitative guidance with its business update for the second quarter of 2026 on or about July 14, 2026. Executive Statement “We are pleased that this customer has chosen SCHMID for the next phase of its HDI-ML and mSAP capacity expansion following completion of the first project. This repeat order reflects the performance and reliability of our InfinityLine H+ and InfinityLine V+ lines in demanding, high-volume industrial production environments. In critical applications such as AI server boards and optical modules, manufacturers cannot compromise on yield, stability, or uptime. Feedback from our customers confirms that our equipment consistently delivers an outstanding production yield of 99% — a crucial advantage when precision is paramount. The momentum in AI-related electronics manufacturing is rapidly converting into real capacity investments. As customers transition from technology development into industrial-scale production, SCHMID is uniquely positioned to support this growth with proven wet-process solutions for mSAP, HDI, and high-end interconnect applications,” said Roland Rettenmeier, Chief Sales Officer of the SCHMID Group. Copies are available on the SEC’s website, www.sec.gov . The Company undertakes no obligation to update these statements for revisions or changes after the date of this release, except as required by law. About the SCHMID Group The SCHMID Group is a global leader in providing solutions mostly for the electronics industry. SCHMID N.V. and Gebr. SCHMID GmbH are headquartered in Freudenstadt, Germany. Founded in 1864, the company currently employs over 800 people worldwide and operates technology centers and production facilities at multiple locations, including Germany and China, along with several global sales and service locations. The Group focuses on developing customized equipment and process solutions mostly for the electronics industry. Our system and process solutions for the production of substrates, printed circuit boards, and other electronic components ensure cutting-edge technology, high yields at low production costs, maximum efficiency, quality, and sustainability through environmentally friendly manufacturing processes.
